title: How to Organize a Refrigerator

content_html:
Organizing a refrigerator is not only about gaining space; it also helps keep food at a safe temperature, prevent raw-meat drips, and use older items first. The layout should preserve appliance airflow and keep the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below.

Check temperature and keep air vents clear

Use a refrigerator thermometer if the display does not reflect the actual compartment temperature. Leave room around internal vents so cold air circulates; packing every gap can create warmer zones.

Keep raw meat low and contained

Place raw meat, poultry, and seafood in a sealed container or tray on a low shelf so drips cannot fall onto ready-to-eat foods. Keep other leaking packages contained as well.

Group foods by use and date

Move opened foods and earlier dates to the front and newer purchases behind them. Zones for breakfast items, leftovers, and cooking ingredients reduce the time spent searching with the door open.

Do not use the door for the most temperature-sensitive foods

The door experiences larger temperature swings than interior shelves. Use it for suitable condiments and drinks; milk, meat, and other highly perishable foods are better kept in colder interior zones.
